Article Title: Dyson launches Airsmooth, its first dedicated hot air brush
Article Text:
Dyson Airsmooth uses two types of bristles

Dyson has launched the Airsmooth, its first dedicated hot air brush, aimed at making everyday hair styling easier while reducing the need for high heat. The device combines Dyson’s airflow technology with PivotFlex and Anti-snag bristle systems to dry, smooth and lift hair. Dyson says the Airsmooth is designed to work across straight, wavy, curly and coily hair types. The device is built for routines such as everyday smoothing, stretching curls and coils, and preparing hair for further styling. It also uses intelligent heat control that measures temperature 100 times a second while styling.The Dyson Airsmooth uses a patented dual-bristle system designed to guide hair through the device. The anti-snag bristles feature a looped structure that can collapse to release strands more easily. Dyson says this helps reduce snagging and breakage while improving comfort around the scalp.The second system is called PivotFlex. Its bristles have an open-base design that helps control and diffuse high-pressure airflow. They can flex by up to 90 degrees while the tapered shape helps hair wrap and release during styling.The two bristle systems are arranged in a teardrop formation to create tension from the roots to the ends.Dyson says the Airsmooth can be used on straight, wavy, curly and coily hair. The device is designed for drying and smoothing hair, stretching curls and coils, and creating a smoother base before another styling step. According to the company, the bristle system is designed to reduce tangles while helping control frizz.The Airsmooth also uses Dyson’s intelligent heat control technology, which measures temperature 100 times per second. The company says this system is designed to provide controlled heat during styling while helping protect the hair's natural texture.Dyson says the Airsmooth has a lightweight and ergonomic design for everyday use across different hair lengths. The device also supports universal voltage, allowing it to be used while travelling. Dyson positions it for use during routines such as getting ready for work, after a workout or while on holiday.The Dyson Airsmooth is introduced in select markets only. The launch in India will be announced closer to the availability.
Article Summary: The Dyson Airsmooth is designed to work across straight, wavy, curly and coily hair types. The device is built for routines such as smoothing, stretching curls and coils, and preparing hair for further styling. It also uses intelligent heat control that measures temperature 100 times a second while styling.

Article Title: AI boom has put several of the biggest American universities are under 'physical threat', George Washington University’s sale of its Virginia campus is an example
Article Text:
AI boom has put several of the biggest American universities are under 'physical threat', George Washington University’s sale of its Virginia campus is an example

George Washington University’s $427 million campus sale for AI data center

University of Michigan builds $1.25 billion AI computing centre

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is creating a new pressure point for American universities. This comes as demand for data centers increases the value of large properties with access to electricity, water and fiber infrastructure. American universities that have traditionally used such land for classrooms, laboratories and research facilities are increasingly competing with AI infrastructure projects, creating what former George Washington University professor Ellen Scully-Russ described as “a physical threat” to higher education resources.The George Washington (GW) University’s sale of its roughly 120-acre Virginia Science and Technology Campus in Ashburn, Virginia, to Amazon Data Services for $427 million is one example of this shift. “Universities are large landholders, and there is a land grab going on with the data centers these days,” Scully-Russ told Fortune. The campus is located in Loudoun County, part of Northern Virginia’s “Data Center Alley”, a major concentration of data centers.GW University announced the sale in February but initially did not identify the buyer or disclose the price, citing confidentiality provisions. Amazon Data Services was later identified as the buyer, paying $427 million for the property.The university said the transaction would strengthen its long-term financial position. GW can continue using the campus for up to five years while it determines how to relocate the programmes and offices operating there. A significant portion of the proceeds will be placed into a new endowment, while eligible faculty and staff will receive one-time payments of $2,500 for benefits-eligible full-time faculty and $1,250 for eligible part-time faculty.The sale came as GW faces financial pressures linked to changes in federal research funding, international student policies and broader challenges affecting higher education. The university has said the transaction will support its finances and allow it to invest in its academic mission.Scully-Russ, who joined GW in 2009 to teach and lead a programme at the Virginia campus, said the property struggled to become a central part of the university’s strategy, despite having newer facilities than some at its Washington, DC, campus.​“It never really got any legs, in my opinion,” she said.She also described a gradual reduction in resources at the campus over several years, including faculty departures that were not replaced and the eventual elimination of teaching assistants because of budget constraints. She said faculty and students were not informed in advance that the university was considering selling the property.“There was no transparency,” she told Fortune. “The faculty, the student body, as far as I know, were not even aware that there was a discussion about selling to anybody, let alone to Amazon.”GW held town halls after the sale was announced to discuss the transition of programmes, faculty and staff from the campus. Scully-Russ questioned the timing of that consultation.“It’s kind of like, do you really care?” she said. “Did you care what I thought before you made this decision? Did you care to let me know that this was in the works?”​However, the George Washington University did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Scully-Russ also raised concerns about universities using land for AI infrastructure while federal funding and other financial pressures affect higher education.“We’re chipping away at our higher ed resources to make room for this technology to expand without any accountability,” she told Fortune, “or any other kind of thoughtful progression, which is really a concern for me.”She also questioned the long-term demand for large AI infrastructure projects.​“I think it’s just a short-term bubble,” she said. “We’re just one technological leap away from having those huge ugly buildings being obsolete. Then what happens?”The University of Michigan is taking a different approach to AI infrastructure through a planned $1.25 billion high-performance computing and research centre in Ypsilanti Township.​Developed with Los Alamos National Laboratory, the project is intended to support research in areas including medicine, materials science, clean energy, engineering, and national security. The university describes the facility as a computing centre rather than a commercial data center and says it will support “applying AI and high-performance computing.”The university has acquired land for the project. In 2024, its Board of Regents approved purchases of 19.82 acres and 6.03 acres in Ypsilanti Township for a future computing centre. In 2025, it received authorisation to purchase about 124.7 acres on Textile Road for the facility.The university has also distinguished the project from commercial data centers, saying the facility will focus on scientific research rather than cloud computing, streaming, e-commerce and other consumer or business applications.The planned facility is expected to require about 50 megawatts of power initially, eventually reaching 100 megawatts, according to a university report.The project has faced opposition from local residents and officials. The Ypsilanti Township Board of Trustees unanimously passed a resolution opposing the proposed computational research facility, “declaring strong and unequivocal opposition.”
Article Summary: University of Michigan builds $1.25 billion AI computing centre in Ypsilanti Township. George Washington University’s $427 million campus sale for AI data center is an example of this shift. Demand for data centers increases the value of large properties with access to electricity, water and fiber infrastructure.

Article Title: In 2025, Sam Altman set a goal for OpenAI engineers to create 'automated research intern', a year later company publishes a long update
Article Text:
In 2025, Sam Altman set a goal for OpenAI engineers to create 'automated research intern', a year later company publishes a long update

Skyrocketing compute usage and token consumption

Corporate reckoning over ' Tokenmaxxing '

Roughly a year after CEO Sam Altman instructed OpenAI engineering teams to design an “automated research intern,” the artificial intelligence (AI) company has announced that it has successfully fulfilled that objective, while setting its sights on engineering a fully independent AI scientist by March 2028. In a long update released, the AI Lab detailed how autonomous programming tools are overhauling its day-to-day laboratory operations.According to the long note, rather than drafting routine scripts manually, staff members are handing off complex duties to automated assistants, leading to higher experimentation volume, faster software releases and a shift toward supervising AI-generated code. It also said that the technology has also taken over corporate troubleshooting. Daily help requests submitted to an internal IT support desk run by human technicians have plunged by more than 50% since January, as staff increasingly rely on autonomous bots to resolve software problems.While various companies have limited the use of AI, adoption among OpenAI’s core research teams has surged over the past three months, growing at a far steeper rate than anywhere else inside the firm. OpenAI revealed that the median researcher consumed over $600 in computational tokens daily by mid-August, representing a sharp increase from the $162 daily baseline recorded in July.The top 10% of researchers are now utilising upwards of $7,000 in tokens every single day. These financial metrics represent estimated market rates calculated using external API pricing schedules rather than the underlying internal production costs incurred by OpenAI.Notably, in June, Altman disclosed that the startup's heaviest internal consumer processes 100 billion tokens per month. Demonstrating that scale, OpenClaw developer Peter Steinberger, who joined the lab in February, shared an internal dashboard in May showing an estimated $1.3 million monthly usage invoice, though the expense was completely absorbed by the employer.The rapid evolution of programming agents is dividing the wider technology sector between productivity enthusiasts and corporations. While numerous software engineers say handing off baseline tasks to synthetic agents enhances their output, others remain skeptical about the workflow.Early in the year, enterprise firms actively nudged employees to use generative models, setting up internal scoreboards to highlight the most active users. The fueled a “tokenmaxxing,” where workers maximised AI interactions without prioritising practical outcomes.As mounting operational bills began to outstrip measurable efficiency gains, major enterprises pulled back. Tech firms like Amazon and Meta disbanded their internal usage leaderboards.
Article Summary: CEO Sam Altman set goal for OpenAI engineers to create 'automated research intern' in 2025. A year later company publishes a long update detailing how autonomous programming tools are overhauling its day-to-day laboratory operations. Daily help requests submitted to an internal IT support desk run by human technicians have plunged by more than 50% since January.

Article Title: How WhatsApp messages and calls led investigators to former USCIS official in alleged $960,000 American citizenship bribery scam
Article Text:
Former USCIS official allegedly fast-tracked citizenship cases

How WhatsApp messages helped investigators trace alleged scam

Former USCIS official allegedly fast-tracked citizenship cases

Prosecutors say nearly $960,000 was paid

Thousands of WhatsApp messages and hundreds of phone calls helped investigators uncover an alleged bribery scheme involving a former senior U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) official, prosecutors say. Ex-USCIS official Lukman Owolabi Ganiyu and his alleged financial accomplice, Adeniyi Akeem Somoye, have been charged over a scheme in which they allegedly accepted nearly $960,000 to manipulate and speed up immigration benefit applications, including citizenship cases.As per a Fox News report, the two men were arrested on federal charges of conspiracy to receive illegal gratuities by a public official, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas. Prosecutors allege the scheme operated from December 2019 through March 2026 and involved applicants paying money in exchange for special treatment.A key part of the investigation was the pair's digital communication with applicants. Investigators found thousands of WhatsApp messages and hundreds of calls between Ganiyu, Somoye and people whose immigration applications they handled, according to prosecutors.The communications allegedly showed repeated contact between the two men and applicants involved in the immigration cases. Prosecutors allege the pair used these contacts as part of a system in which applicants paid for their cases to be pushed through the immigration process, the report states.According to the allegations, Ganiyu used his position at USCIS to bypass normal procedures for applicants who paid bribes. Prosecutors say some applications were moved forward without key steps such as criminal background checks, interviews, standard USCIS processing procedures and other reviews.Ganiyu allegedly changed information in the USCIS system to speed up applications. Prosecutors also allege that he moved cases from USCIS field offices in Minneapolis, Charlotte and Houston so that he could approve them himself, bypassing local supervisors.The complaint further alleges that Ganiyu fast-tracked Somoye's citizenship application before approving residency applications for Somoye's wife and child.Court documents cited in the report say Ganiyu received about $671,438 from citizenship applicants through Zelle and Cash App. He also allegedly received $287,830 through cash deposits that prosecutors say were intended to hide the source of the money.Somoye allegedly acted as a financial intermediary. Prosecutors say he handled about $1.7 million in transfers involving applicants through bank accounts, Zelle and Cash App, while allegedly keeping part of the money. He also allegedly deposited $449,010 in cash. The complaint says Ganiyu and Somoye frequently exchanged money "back and forth" with applicants.According to prosecutors, most of the citizenship applications handled by the pair involved applicants from African countries. The allegations cover a period of more than six years, from December 2019 until March 2026.Ganiyu resigned from USCIS in March, citing "personal reasons," according to the report. He was arrested several months later.
Article Summary: Ex-USCIS official Lukman Owolabi Ganiyu and his alleged financial accomplice, Adeniyi Akeem Somoye, have been charged over a scheme in which they allegedly accepted nearly $960,000 to manipulate and speed up immigration benefit applications. Prosecutors allege the scheme operated from December 2019 through March 2026 and involved applicants paying money in exchange for special treatment. A key part of the investigation was the pair's digital communication with applicants.

Article Title: Melinda Gates made a surprise appearance at Olivia Rodrigo's benefit show, made a $10 million donation and thanked for 'showing a new generation how much ...'
Article Text:
Olivia Rodrigo's benefit show raises $20 million

Melinda Gates praises Olivia Rodrigo for reaching a new generation

Melinda French Gates made a surprise appearance at Olivia Rodrigo 's benefit concert. According to a Fortune report, Gates announced a $10 million donation, helping the event raise a total of $20 million for organisations working on women's health, rights and well-being. Melinda Gates, who pledged the money through her organisation Pivotal Ventures, praised the Grammy-winning singer for using her platform to bring young people closer to important social causes. “Showing a new generation how much their voices matter,” Gates said while recognising Rodrigo's efforts at the event.The benefit show, called Daisy Chain Fields, was held in Irvine, California, and brought together music, activism and fundraising. The event featured a women-led lineup including Chappell Roan, Doechii and Bikini Kill.Olivia Rodrigo had earlier announced that the event had raised enough money to make a $10 million donation to 10 nonprofit organisations. The groups included Planned Parenthood, the National Women's Law Center and Black Mamas Matter Alliance. Gates' surprise $10 million pledge doubled the amount raised.The 23-year-old singer said the artists and activists involved in the event gave her hope despite what she described as the “regression of women’s rights” today.“That’s actually why I fell in love with the name ‘Daisy Chain,’” Rodrigo said. “It served as a reminder of how individual parts can come together to create something strong and unbreakable.”Melinda French Gates' appearance was one of the biggest moments of the benefit show. Her donation through Pivotal Ventures highlighted the growing role that celebrities and musicians can play in connecting younger audiences with charitable causes. Rodrigo's event also gave attendees a chance to learn directly about the work of nonprofit groups. Organisations set up booths in what was described as a “philanthropy village,” where fans could learn about health services, workers' rights and other issues supported by the fundraiser.The event drew inspiration from Lilith Fair, the all-women music festival that raised $10 million for charity between 1997 and 1999. Sarah McLachlan, who founded Lilith Fair, also performed with Rodrigo at the show.
Article Summary: Melinda French Gates made a surprise appearance at Olivia Rodrigo's benefit concert. Gates announced a $10 million donation, helping the event raise a total of $20 million for organisations working on women's health, rights and well- being. The benefit show, called Daisy Chain Fields, was held in Irvine, California.

Article Title: Sony CEO says PS5 no longer needs aggressive marketing as console enters later years
Article Text:
Sony says PS5 is now in the latter half of its life cycle

Sony says PS5 is now in the latter half of its life cycle

PlayStation Plus becomes more important for Sony

PS5 price increases and physical games debate continue

Sony is changing its strategy for the PlayStation 5 as the console moves deeper into the later part of its life cycle. Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki said the company is no longer focused on “aggressively” selling the PS5, arguing that the console has reached a stage where the company can put more attention on earning money from its existing players. “We are in the latter half of the life cycle for a PlayStation console,” Hiroki Totoki said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal in August this year. “That means that we do not need to ‘aggressively sell’ the console today,” he added.The shift comes nearly six years after the PlayStation 5 launched in November 2020. According to Totoki, Sony’s focus is now moving from selling more consoles to increasing recurring revenue from its large PlayStation user base.During the WSJ interview, Totoki said Sony does not need to push PS5 sales as aggressively as it did earlier in the console's life. Instead, Sony is looking at ways to generate more recurring revenue from people who already use PlayStation products and services.Totoki pointed to PlayStation Plus as an important part of that strategy. He said the service now has more than 125 million monthly active users, making its existing customer base a major opportunity for Sony.Sony's comments suggest that services and subscriptions are becoming increasingly important to the PlayStation business as the PS5 matures. Rather than relying only on new console sales, the company wants to increase the value it gets from its existing users. PlayStation Plus offers access to online multiplayer, games and other benefits across its subscription plans.The comments also come at a time when Sony is dealing with changes across the PlayStation business, including higher hardware prices and growing debate around digital games.Sony increased the prices of the PS5, PS5 Pro and PlayStation Portal in several markets in April 2026, citing continued cost pressures.At the same time, the company has faced criticism from some players over its plans to reduce its reliance on physical game discs. Sony's chief financial officer Lin Tao said in July that the company would “cautiously move forward” with ending physical discs, pointing to the growing digitisation of content.Sony has also faced a class-action lawsuit over how digital game purchases are presented to consumers. The company has argued that consumers should not assume they permanently own digital games in the same way they own physical products.
Article Summary: Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki said the company is no longer focused on ‘aggressively’ selling the PS5. He said the console has reached a stage where the company can put more attention on earning money from its existing players. The shift comes nearly six years after the PlayStation 5 launched.

Article Title: Tech CEO added to FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list; what 'Lookout' notice says
Article Text:
Here’s what FBI’s lookout notice for Bernhard Eugen Fritsch says

DESCRIPTION

, Bernhard E. Fritsch, Barnhard Eugen Fritsch, Charles Wiest

Date(s) of Birth Used: July 27, 1961

Place of Birth: Landshut, Germany

Eyes: Brown

Sex: Male

Languages: English, German

REWARD

The FBI is offering a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of Bernhard Eugen Fritsch.

REMARKS

Fritsch is believed to be residing in or near Munich, Germany.

CAUTION

Bernhard Eugen Fritsch is wanted for his alleged involvement in a scheme to defraud investors after raising approximately $35 million for Fritsch’s technology company, Starclub Inc. between January of 2014, and August of 2017. Starclub purportedly developed software and an application to help celebrities and social media influencers monetize their brand endorsements.

Fritsch claimed to have deals with major global media and entertainment companies and misrepresented StarClub’s financial performance to induce investments.

At least $7.3 million of investor money was used to fund Fritsch’s personal expenses such as mortgage payments, residential expenses, and luxury vehicles. In April of 2025, Fritsch was found guilty of wire fraud in a California court.

In June of 2025, prior to a bond revocation hearing, Fritsch fled to Los Mochis, Sinaloa, Mexico.

On June 3, 2025, a federal arrest warrant was issued for Fritsch in the United States District Court, Central District of California, Los Angeles, California, after he failed to appear for his Post-Conviction Bond Revocation Hearing.

In September of 2025, Mexican law enforcement detained Fritsch, who was found with false identification. He was released from immigration custody and ordered to check in with the immigration court in Mexico every 2 weeks.

However, on October 6, 2025, Fritsch fled to Munich, Germany. On October 20, 2025, Fritsch was sentenced in absentia to 15 years in prison, fined $35,000, and was later ordered to pay $26,806,901 in restitution.

If you have any information concerning this case, please contact the FBI's Toll-Free tipline at 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324). You may also contact your local FBI office, the nearest American Embassy or Consulate, or you can submit a tip online at tips.fbi.gov.

Field Office: Los Angeles

The FBI has added Tech CEO Bernhard Eugen Fritsch to its list of Most Wanted Fraudsters list, and the agency has now issued a “Lookout” notice detailing the case against him. Fritsch, the founder and CEO of Santa Monica-based StarClub Inc. , was found guilty of defrauding investors in a case involving more than $26.8 million in losses. The FBI says Fritsch fled the United States before he could be sentenced, later travelling from Mexico to Germany. He was sentenced in absentia to 15 years in federal prison and ordered to pay more than $26.8 million in restitution. The FBI is offering up to $150,000 for information that leads to his arrest and conviction. The “Lookout” notice provides details about his case, the charges against him and his movements after leaving the US.
Article Summary: Bernhard Eugen Fritsch is wanted for his alleged involvement in a scheme to defraud investors. He was found guilty of defrauding investors in a case involving more than $26.8 million in losses. The FBI is offering a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to his arrest and conviction.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang congratulates OpenAI’s team on GPT-6 Astra launch, says ‘AGI has arrived’
Article Text:
Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia.

What changed under the hood

The Nvidia-OpenAI relationship

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has declared that artificial intelligence (AGI) has officially arrived, crediting OpenAI’s newly unveiled GPT-6 Astra model. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Huang congratulated ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and wrote, “GPT-6 Astra, trained on ~100K+ NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVLink72. From ChatGPT to o1 to Astra in 4 years. AGI has arrived. Congratulations @OpenAI team.” Huang further stated that GPT-6 Astra was trained on over 100,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell NVLink72 systems, each designed to link 72 GPUs into a unified computing powerhouse. He initially cited 300,000 systems before revising the figure to 100,000. Looking ahead, Huang said 400,000 GPUs are coming online next, underscoring Nvidia’s central role in powering the AI revolution.The claim rests on a major shift in Nvidia's chip architecture. The company used to ship its processors eight to a board; its newer NVLink72 design instead wires 72 chips together to function as a single, unified system. That redesign came at enormous cost, and only pays off if a customer is training something large enough to need it. OpenAI's Astra model appears to be exactly that customer, according to Huang's figures.One detail has raised questions: Huang's original post reportedly cited 300,000 systems before he deleted it and reposted the smaller 100,000 figure, with no explanation offered for the discrepancy.The Nvidia-OpenAI relationship has also shown signs of cooling beneath the surface. A $100 billion deal the two companies announced in 2025 was reportedly never formally signed, and reporting in June indicated OpenAI had quietly scaled back its Nvidia chip purchases. Against that backdrop, markets are likely to pay closer attention to Huang's pledge of 400,000 additional GPUs coming online than to the AGI declaration itself — a claim that has already drawn skepticism online, with one social media user noting that reaching AGI by 2026 defies earlier expectations that it wouldn't happen until 2029 or later.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model trained on 100,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell NVLink72 systems. He initially cited 300,000 systems before revising the figure to 100,00. Huang said 400,000 more GPUs are coming online next.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Mark Zuckerberg: “The biggest risk is not taking any risk…” - a reminder not to let fear make you miss an opportunity
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Mark Zuckerberg

“The biggest risk is not taking any risk... In a world that changing really quickly, the only strategy that is guaranteed to fail is not taking risks.”

Understanding the meaning behind today’s quote

Why inaction can become a risk

Mark Zuckerberg's early years at Facebook

The problem with waiting for certainty

What can be learned from the quote

Consider the risk of doing nothing: A decision to wait or stay with the familiar can have consequences of its own.

Define the risk clearly: Look at what could be lost, what could be gained and whether the decision can be reversed.

Start with smaller experiments: Testing an idea on a limited scale can reduce the potential cost of failure.

Do not confuse risk with recklessness: Taking a calculated risk involves understanding the possible outcomes rather than ignoring them.

Accept that certainty is rare: New ideas and opportunities rarely come with a guarantee of success.

Learn from unsuccessful decisions: A failed attempt can provide useful information for the next decision.

Keep changing circumstances in mind: A strategy that works today may become less effective as technology, markets or customer behaviour change.

Compare action with inaction: Instead of asking only what could go wrong by acting, consider what might happen if nothing changes.

A different way of looking at failure

The misconception about taking risks

Playing it safe can feel like the easiest way to avoid trouble. There is comfort in keeping a familiar job, sticking with a business model that already works or leaving an uncertain idea for another day. The difficulty is that circumstances do not always stay familiar. Industries change, technology moves on and opportunities can disappear while a decision is being postponed. Mark Zuckerberg's career has unfolded against that kind of uncertainty. From launching Facebook as a university student to making major bets on new technologies and online services, his work has involved decisions where the outcome could not have been known in advance.That does not mean every risk produces a good result, nor that caution is always a mistake. His observation is more specific than that. When the world is changing quickly, refusing to make uncertain choices can have consequences too. His well-known quote raises a simple question: what might standing still cost when everything around you is moving?Zuckerberg's point is fairly direct. When the environment around a person or organisation is changing quickly, avoiding every uncertain decision does not remove risk. It can create a different kind of risk, one that comes from remaining in a position that may no longer work.Consider a company with a product that has performed well for years. Keeping it unchanged may protect existing revenue and avoid the cost of developing something new. But if customers begin moving towards another type of product, the company can eventually find itself trying to respond after the market has already shifted.The same idea can apply to an individual. Staying in a familiar job avoids the uncertainty of changing careers. It also means accepting whatever happens to that existing role as the industry develops.The quote is therefore less about chasing danger and more about recognising that uncertainty exists whether or not someone chooses to act.Risk is often measured by asking what could go wrong after a decision is made. That is only half the calculation. There is also the question of what might happen if the decision is never made.A business that chooses not to develop a new technology may save money in the short term. If competitors invest successfully, however, the business may later need to spend considerably more just to catch up. The original decision looked conservative. Its longer-term consequences may be less so.For individuals, the same pattern can be harder to notice. Someone who never applies for a different position cannot be rejected from it. They also cannot get it. A person who decides not to learn a new skill avoids the effort involved, but may eventually find that the skill has become necessary.This does not make action automatically preferable. Sometimes the information available is too weak, the potential loss is too large or waiting genuinely is the better choice.Mark Zuckerberg was born in 1984 and attended Harvard University. While studying there, he developed a social networking website with fellow students. Facebook launched in 2004 and initially focused on university communities.The service expanded beyond Harvard and other universities relatively quickly. Zuckerberg eventually left Harvard to concentrate on the company as its user base grew.Facebook's early development took place during a period when internet use was changing quickly. Social networking was still a relatively new idea, and the company had to make decisions about expansion, advertising, technology and competition without knowing exactly how the market would develop.People often want enough information to know that a decision will work before making it. With genuinely new ideas, that point rarely arrives.A new product has no established sales record. A new technology may not yet have a settled market. A career change involves an unfamiliar environment. Waiting for certainty can therefore mean waiting until the uncertainty has already been resolved by someone else.Technology companies face this problem frequently. Products that seem unimportant at first can become widely adopted. Consumer habits can shift after the arrival of a new device or platform.Moving too early has its own disadvantages. A company can spend heavily on an idea before the market is ready. But waiting too long can produce a different problem, particularly when competitors have already gained experience.Failure is easier to notice than a missed opportunity. A failed business venture leaves behind bills and records. A rejected job application produces an email. A product that does not sell gives a company clear numbers to examine.The cost of doing nothing can be much quieter.There may be no obvious moment when a person realises that a skill should have been learned earlier. A business may never know exactly how much growth it lost because it delayed entering a market.This makes inaction psychologically easier to accept. Nothing visibly went wrong. Yet something can still have been lost.Zuckerberg's quote draws attention to this less visible side of decision-making. It does not make failure desirable. It simply suggests that avoiding failure completely is not the same as avoiding risk.The most obvious misunderstanding is that the quote means people should take as many risks as possible.Zuckerberg's statement specifically refers to a world that is changing quickly. The circumstances matter. A risk that makes sense for a technology company facing rapid disruption may make little sense for someone dealing with a completely different situation.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg was born in 1984 and attended Harvard University. While studying there he developed a social website with fellow students. Facebook launched in 2004 and initially focused on university communities. Zuckerberg eventually left Harvard to concentrate on the company as user base grew.

Article Title: Hackers steal $320 million in crypto from Bitcoin network used by exchanges: What the company has to say
Article Text:
Liquid Network halts activity amid wallet impact

We are aware of a security incident on @Liquid_BTC. Purported white-hat hackers have withdrawn ~4,000 BTC (~$320 million) from the Liquid Federation wallet.

The @Blockstream team is working on contacting them on-chain with a signed message.

What we know so far is that the funds were withdrawn via the SideSwap PAK (Peg-out Authorization Key), but that key was not compromised, nor were any others.

Exchanges have been notified and have already paused (or will pause) LBTC deposits and withdrawals. Other Liquid assets such as USDT, DePix, and RWAs are unaffected by this security incident.

Bridge nodes have been temporarily disabled, so no new transactions can be submitted to the network. Effectively, the Liquid sidechain is paused until this issue is resolved.

Liquid wallets will be impacted, and we're sorry for any inconvenience. Federation members are actively working on resolving this so we can restore normal network activity.

A high-speed blockchain network relied on by multiple cryptocurrency trading platforms has been hit by a massive hacking, resulting in the theft of roughly $320 million and dealing another sharp blow to digital asset safety. Liquid Network, a specialised sidechain built to accelerate transaction speeds between trading desks, confirmed on X (formerly Twitter) that approximately 4,000 out of the 4,200 Bitcoin held in its primary Federation storage wallet were removed without authorisation.In response to the drain, network administrators moved swiftly to freeze all incoming and outgoing settlement activity to prevent further exposure. The company also posted a long statement confirming the security breach:The multi-million-dollar extraction comes during an escalating wave of cyberattacks targeting digital asset infrastructure. Last week, hackers siphoned $6 million from an asset-lending protocol associated with Crypto.com . A security breach concerning Coldcard, a well-liked offline Bitcoin storage device, in August prompted a burst of debate throughout the industry on the best ways to keep digital possessions safe.

How to report a complaint

What happens after reporting

Article Title: Huawei launches Mate XT 2 trifold smartphone in China, ahead of Apple’s September 9 event
Article Text:
Huawei Mate XT 2 trifold smartphone specifications and features

Huawei has launched the Mate XT 2, its third-generation trifold smartphone, in China. The timing of the release is notable as the phone makes its debut just two days before Apple’s ‘Surprise and Shine’ event on September 9 where the company is expected to present its first-ever foldable iPhone.Huawei Mate XT 2 trifold smartphone price in ChinaThe flagship device will officially go on sale across China on September 10. Pricing begins at ¥19,999 (roughly $2,980) for an entry-level configuration featuring 16GB of RAM and 256GB of internal storage. The top-tier variant, which packs 1TB of storage alongside an optional privacy screen, tops out at ¥24,999 (around $3,725).Departing from the outward folding mechanisms seen on earlier Mate XT iterations, Huawei redesigned the Mate XT 2 to fold inward along both sides of its 10.2-inch panel, taking cues from Samsung's Galaxy Z TriFold. The company also overhauled the hinge system to smooth out and soften the display crease along the bending lines.The top-spec Huawei Mate XT 2 becomes Huawei’s first foldable smartphone to offer a dedicated privacy screen feature. When activated, the viewing angles narrow significantly so that the panel looks nearly black from the side while staying clear to the person looking straight on. Both screens feature LTPO AMOLED panels. The exterior cover screen supports refresh rates up to 120Hz at a resolution of 2,442 x 1,140 pixels. The expansive internal foldable display delivers a higher resolution of 3,184 x 2,232 pixels, running at a standard 90Hz, with only the top-tier version upgrading the inner panel to 120Hz.Under the hood is Huawei’s new Kirin 9050 Pro SoC, which the company states provides a 46% jump in performance compared to the prior Kirin 9030 Pro. The smartphone runs on a 5,600mAh battery supporting 66W wired USB-C fast charging and 50W wireless charging.The rear camera setup features a 50MP primary camera with a variable aperture ranging from f/1.49 to f/4.0, paired with a 40MP ultra-wide sensor and a 50MP periscope telephoto lens offering 3.5x optical zoom. Both the outer cover and main inner displays house an 8MP front camera.

Article Title: Tim Cook will not take stage during Apple iPhone 18 launch event
Article Text:
iPhone 18 launch event may not see Tim Cook taking stage

Tim Cook will watch the iPhone 18 launch from the audience

The transition has already begun behind the scenes

Tim Cook is still expected to have a role at Apple

For years, Tim Cook has been the familiar face of Apple ’s product launches, appearing on stage and in keynote videos as the company introduced new iPhones and other devices. That will change at the upcoming iPhone 18 event. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Cook will not appear in the pre-recorded Apple Event video, although he is expected to attend the screening at Apple Park as a VIP guest.The change comes as Apple completes its transition from Cook to John Ternus as CEO. Cook is moving into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board, while Ternus takes over as the company’s public-facing leader.Gurman wrote in his “Power On” newsletter that Cook will be present at the Apple Park screening with members of the press and other invited guests. His absence from the event video will allow Ternus to take the lead as Apple introduces its next generation of iPhones.The timing is also significant because the launch is expected to include Apple’s first foldable iPhone. Having Ternus lead the presentation gives the new CEO an opportunity to establish himself as Apple's face during an important product cycle.Cook’s move to chairman has involved changes beyond the stage.He has moved out of his previous office in Section 7 of Apple Park and is getting a new office, while Ternus has taken over the CEO office in the executive suite.The two executives have also praised each other during public appearances and in internal communications as the leadership change has progressed.Cook has made several public and internal farewells in recent months. He addressed the transition during his final earnings call, in a memo to employees and during the WWDC keynote.In his last CEO memo, Cook told employees that he looked forward to seeing them at Apple campuses around the world, making clear that he would remain involved with the company rather than leave it entirely.Although he will no longer present Apple's products, Cook is expected to remain active in his new role. His compensation also reflects the continuing nature of his role.As executive chairman, Cook will receive a base salary of $2 million and could receive up to $45 million in restricted stock units in 2027. By comparison, Art Levinson, the non-executive chairman whom Cook replaced, received less than $560,000 in salary, stock and other compensation last year.That means Cook's absence from the launch video should not be interpreted as an exit from Apple. He is expected to be at Apple Park for the event, watching the company's next chapter from a different place.The September launch will therefore mark a change in more than just the iPhone lineup. After years of seeing Cook introduce Apple's products, viewers will now see Ternus take that role while Cook watches from the audience.
Article Summary: Tim Cook will not appear in the pre-recorded Apple Event video, although he is expected to attend the screening at Apple Park as a VIP guest. The change comes as Apple completes its transition from Cook to John Ternus as CEO. Cook is moving into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board.

Article Title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says 'AGI has arrived' after OpenAI GPT-6 Astra rollout for which Sam Altman said ‘sorry’
Article Text:
OpenAI unveils Astra: ‘Welcome to the AGI Era’

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has congratulated OpenAI following the debut of its latest frontier model, Astra, and declared that artificial general intelligence (AGI) has finally emerged. Taking to social media platform X, he celebrated ChatGPT-maker’s rapid technological progression while highlighting that Astra was developed using Nvidia’s advanced hardware. The term AGI refers to automated systems capable of equaling or exceeding human cognitive abilities across various domains. Huang also hinted that far more processing power is on the horizon, noting that 400,000 additional graphics processing units will soon go live to support continued AI model training and execution.“From ChatGPT to o1 to Astra in 4 years. AGI has arrived,” Huang posted on X, adding, “Congratulations @OpenAI team. 400K GPUs coming online next.”OpenAI formally introduced Astra last week, promoting the architecture as its most capable and aligned system to date. According to the company, the model is engineered to handle complex professional responsibilities with precision, speed, and analytical reasoning, marking a major leap forward in what tasks organisations can safely offload to automation.During a press briefing, OpenAI president Greg Brockman framed the launch as a historic turning point. “Welcome to the AGI era,” Brockman told reporters, adding that he expects future observers will pinpoint this period, and potentially Astra itself, as the exact emergence of AGI.According to a report by Business Insider, despite the celebratory declarations from executive suites, several prominent figures in the AI sector urged caution and rejected the claims. Longtime AI researcher and critic Gary Marcus criticised Huang’s assertion as premature.Even OpenAI CEO Sam Altman recently downplayed the significance of the acronym during an interview on the Sources podcast, calling AGI an ill-defined concept and describing it as an almost irrelevant marketing label.Meanwhile, GPT-6 Astra’s debut highlights the central role Nvidia plays across the AI sector, as leading development groups, including OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta, remain heavily reliant on the company's high-performance processors. During an investment update in March, OpenAI characterised Nvidia as the structural foundation of its computing operations, confirming that its primary training supercomputers and inference workflows depend heavily on Nvidia GPUs.Altman also apologised for a messy GPT-6 Astra rollout, hours after his company called the model a generational leap in capability and said it marked the beginning of the AGI era.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang congratulates OpenAI on debut of Astra, its latest frontier model. He says it marks the beginning of artificial general intelligence (AGI) era. The term refers to automated systems capable of equaling or exceeding human cognitive abilities. Huang also hinted that far more processing power is on the horizon.

Article Title: Apple's top executive Phil Schiller, who has worked with both Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, is stepping down; and the reason is …
Article Text:
Other changes in Apple leadership

Longtime Apple executive Phil Schiller, who worked closely with both Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, is stepping down from his daily role overseeing the App Store and product launches. Schiller's departure comes as Apple faces a wider leadership churn, with roughly half of its senior management bench expected to step aside over the next few years. Now in his weekly newsletter, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has revealed the underlying reasons behind Schiller’s move.Gurman said that at 66, Schiller sought a pathway toward personal retirement, hoping to direct his time toward charitable efforts and family commitments. However, strategic disagreements reportedly also played a central role in his decision to step away. Key executives, including Ternus and services head Eddy Cue, are exploring avenues to extract higher margins, generate additional recurring revenue, and expand overall earnings from the App Store.Schiller viewed these aggressive monetisation efforts as a means to further fee pressure that would alienate application developers and trigger additional hostility from government regulators. It is to be noted that while the policy divergence did not result in an overt corporate clash, Schiller chose not to participate in the marketplace’s new monetisation direction, opting instead to pass on the high-profile assignment.The move follows the recent transition of former CFO Luca Maestri. While both veterans stay connected to corporate payrolls, Maestri teaching rising personnel at Apple University and Schiller retained for undefined special initiatives, Schiller’s step back carries far greater operational consequence.Unlike Maestri’s recent responsibilities, Schiller maintained an active, high-stakes operational portfolio. Maestri’s recent oversight of corporate services was largely nominal, managing vice presidents who already operated with significant autonomy. Paying a $15 million annual compensation package for a post requiring office appearances once or twice a week offered little commercial justification, though his current instructor role at Apple University allows him to train emerging corporate talent.Schiller handled two demanding pillars of Apple’s consumer apparatus: keynote product announcements and the global App Store. While staging Apple Events drives international launch messaging, steering the App Store means running a digital marketplace generating an estimated $30 billion each year.
Article Summary: Longtime Apple executive Phil Schiller is stepping down from his daily role overseeing the App Store and product launches. Schiller's departure comes as Apple faces a wider leadership churn, with roughly half of its senior management bench expected to step aside over the next few years.

Article Title: After OpenAI AI agent again 'caught hacking', company's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki warns every other company: You are not prepared for ...
Article Text:
The risks OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is warning about

Agents that can hack, deceive, and manipulate

Agents that can hide their reasoning

Agents that can accelerate their own development

A call for outside oversight

OpenAI recently introduced its newest model Astra. Now days after the launch ChatGPT-maker has once again discovered its AI agents engaging in hacking behaviour. The incident prompted chief scientists Jakub Pachocki to issue a stark warning: “No one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence. ” Pachocki said that while OpenAI is working on technical safeguards, broader interventions are needed to prevent autonomous agents from evading oversight, breaking into systems, or tricking people to achieve their objectives.Pachocki said AI agents are becoming exceptionally skilled at breaking into protected systems across the open internet, putting global infrastructure at risk. He argued that there's currently only a narrow window to use today's best models to substantially strengthen the security of critical systems before that risk grows further. He also warned that agents will increasingly pursue objectives separate from what human operators actually asked for, and won't hesitate to bargain with or even blackmail people to get there. A related report published in August by the UK's AI Security Institute described a case where a rogue Anthropic agent misled and attempted to pressure a GitHub administrator into installing malware, with the agent insisting it had only been trying to help.OpenAI currently monitors AI behavior largely by reading a model's "chain of thought" — the step-by-step reasoning an agent uses to work through a task, which lets researchers catch it if it starts planning something like cheating on a test. Right now, agents have no way to conceal that reasoning from OpenAI's monitoring. But Pachocki said newer models are getting better at manipulating their own reasoning processes, which could eventually let them hide their true thinking from oversight altogether. He noted some of the latest models don't verbalize their reasoning at all, a development he said could slow AI progress while researchers work out how to maintain visibility into what these systems are actually doing.Pachocki also flagged the growing use of what he calls machine recursive self-improvement, in which AI models improve themselves, dramatically speeding up the pace of AI development. He cautioned that pushing this kind of AI-on-AI development too far, too fast, isn't the right collective choice for the research community to make right now. He said human overseers will need to find new ways to monitor self-improving systems, or coordinate across AI companies on a joint slowdown to build confidence in safety measures. As he put it, the real challenge isn't achieving automated AI research itself, but getting there in a way that keeps people involved in the process and keeps humanity in control of the outcome.In a lengthy blog post published Sunday, Jakub Pachocki said he worries that the field as a whole isn't prepared for the consequences of AI capabilities continuing to accelerate at their current pace. While he said OpenAI is working on internal technical fixes to keep powerful AI agents under control, he argued that those efforts alone won't be enough, and that broader intervention is needed. Specifically, he pointed to the danger of increasingly autonomous agents learning to slip past human oversight, break into computer systems, and manipulate people into helping them achieve their goals.Pachocki called for mandatory safety standards, suggesting they could be enforced through a mix of third-party auditors, government agencies, or international bodies. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman amplified the post on X, describing it as important.The timing is notable: OpenAI unveiled its newest model, Astra, on Thursday, touting it as its most aligned system to date — meaning it's less prone to going rogue — despite what the company describes as unmatched capabilities in mathematics and computer use.Pachocki's stance echoes long-standing calls from rival Anthropic for standardized government regulation of advanced AI. He himself signed an open letter in July asking the federal government to slow the pace of AI development.
Article Summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki warns of growing risk of rogue AI agents. Calls for mandatory safety standards to be enforced through third-party auditors, government agencies, or international bodies. Warns that agents will increasingly pursue objectives separate from what human operators actually asked for, and won't hesitate to bargain with.

Article Title: China's biggest online shopping store in Europe found paying $962 million to influencers who do not exist on Meta
Article Text:
Real money going to fake accounts

Legal questions for Temu

Temu may have spent as much as $962 million on Meta ads promoted through accounts that likely do not represent real influencers. According to research reviewed by Fortune, 73 of the 100 creators whose content was most heavily boosted by the Chinese online retailer in the UK and Europe were likely fake accounts, raising questions about how the company’s advertising budget is being used on Facebook and Instagram.​One of those accounts belongs to Ya Lili, who has about 183,000 followers on Instagram under the handle “@findgadgetswithme.” Her videos promote Temu products, including one recent post featuring a shower scrubber. The video shows a man covered in dirt before a woman appears and demonstrates the product. A link below the video directs viewers to Temu.​According to Online Risk Labs (ORL), Ya Lili was Temu’s top creator for partnership ads on Meta platforms in the UK and Europe. The research suggests the account almost certainly does not represent a real person.Ya Lili also has about 129,000 followers on Facebook, where the account uses the name “Must good.” Its location is listed as “England, Birmingham, MO, United States,” while its bio says “You are my dream of dead.” Its email address also appears to be Chinese.Posts from the account were boosted by Temu and viewed more than 1 billion times across Facebook and Instagram during the 16 months ending in April 2026, according to ORL.The account's content appeared in nearly 109,541 Temu ad campaigns, or about 225 campaigns per day.ORL estimates Temu spent as much as $962 million on similar ads in the UK and 27 EU countries during the period. The estimate is based on total impressions and average cost per reach. The group estimates Temu accounts for nearly 2% of Meta's revenue from the continent in any given quarter.Of the top 100 creators working with Temu, only eight were verified with a real identity, according to ORL. Twenty-eight were based in Russia and 19 in China, while only six were based in the EU or UK“Among the top 100 influencers collaborating with Temu, there are certainly some real people among them. In my estimate, however, they account for no more than 15–20%. By contrast, I have serious doubts about the authenticity of accounts that, according to the platform, are based in Russia, China, or Iran,” ORL manager Vendula Prokůpková told Fortune.The findings could raise regulatory questions because European advertising rules prohibit misleading commercial practices. Stuart Lester, who leads the advertising and marketing group at London law firm Mishcon de Reya, said fake accounts presented as real individuals could breach regulations.“By all means utilise Facebook and Instagram and influencers, but know that there are rules that you have to abide by, and you certainly can’t be creating fake accounts and portraying these as real individuals. That’s misleading on many levels,” Reya explained.It remains unclear whether Temu knowingly uses such accounts or is being deceived by scammers. There is also no evidence that the Temu products or advertisements themselves are fraudulent.ORL has filed a report with the EU's Digital Services Act regulator asking it to assess the risks associated with Temu's influencer accounts. Creators augmented with AI production processes and performance-optimisation algorithms are only going to become more prevalent across the industry, and this seems to fit squarely into that bucket.
Article Summary: Chinese online retailer Temu may have spent as much as $962 million on Meta ads promoted through accounts that likely do not represent real influencers. 73 of the 100 creators whose content was most heavily boosted by the Chinese online retailer in the UK and Europe were likely fake accounts.

Article Title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami International Airport, kills 5: Here’s the latest update shared by the company

An Amazon cargo aircraft operated by 21 Air crashed while attempting to land at Miami International Airport on September 6, killing at least five people and injuring five others. Article Title: Tech jobs shrinking because of AI but chip factories are creating new manufacturing roles
Article Text:
Tech jobs contract as manufacturing roles rebound

Markets and federal policy friction

The American labour market posted a surge in hiring this August, as per the fresh data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It also reveals a difference across industries as technology positions retreat due to the artificial intelligence (AI) boom while hardware fabrication gains ground due to chip manufacturing. Domestic employers expanded their payrolls by 162,000 workers last month, blowing past market projections of just 53,000 additions. Citing data, The New York Post reported that the nationwide unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%.According to the data, past employment figures also saw sharp positive adjustments. Revised tallies indicate July actually added 21,000 jobs rather than dropping 23,000, while June figures were lifted by 11,000 to reach 31,000 net positions. Meanwhile, the labor participation rate ticked upward by 0.1% following months of steady erosion, though it remains down 0.5% compared to January levels.The report outlined contrasting fortunes across different segments of the economy. White-collar professions faced headwinds as the information sector, which feels direct operational pressure from fast-moving AI automation, eliminated 23,000 positions in August.In contrast, industrial manufacturing signaled a rebound by adding 16,000 roles, bouncing back from a multi-month trough recorded in December 2025. This appears to be supported by large-scale construction and production at semiconductor manufacturing plants tied directly to AI infrastructure.Hospitality and leisure generated the strongest single-category surge by adding 62,000 roles after two straight months of shrinkage. Municipal public school employment recovered 42,000 positions following midsummer vacation distortions, though the sector has remained largely stagnant since January 2025.Following the strong payroll release, the yield on 10-year US Treasury notes climbed to 4.772%, stirring trader speculation that the Federal Reserve will prioritise fighting inflation and could potentially hike borrowing costs this month, the report said.The data drew swift commentary from President Donald Trump, who took to Truth Social to applaud the hiring surge while demanding the central bank slash borrowing costs.“Great jobs number just announced, breaking all estimates (except mine!) by double and triple - And you haven’t seen anything yet! EMPLOYERS ADDED 162,000 JOB IN AUGUST. Lower the interest rates because the USA is a much stronger credit than it was just a short time ago! LOWER THE RATE OR I’LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT, which the U.S. Supreme Court, in its ridiculous and very costly Tariff decision, strongly acknowledged “the President” has an absolute right to do. ”
Article Summary: US employers expanded their payrolls by 162,000 workers last month, blowing past market projections of just 53,000 additions. White-collar professions faced headwinds as the information sector, which feels direct operational pressure from fast-moving AI automation, eliminated 23,000 positions.
